memberships.parsedDescription: Thank You, Stillman is a Super 8 mm travel diary from a 2021 visit to Brownsville, Texas. The film is made of images from the gulf coast—an abandoned waterpark, a lighthouse, marine debris, and newly erected rockets—set against the lyrics of Gene Autry’s That Silver Haired Daddy of Mine. Brownsville was founded by Charles Stillman, the great-great grandfather of writer and director Whit Stillman. Without Brownsville my paternal family would not exist, and neither would this film.

memberships.parsedDescription: To Dress a Wound is a poetry-driven experimental short exploring Black girl grief, rage, and daydreams, examining the emotional weight Black women and femmes carry under racial capitalism and patriarchy, and tracing how these histories live within the body across generations. memberships.parsedDescription: Passing through multiple layers of transformation on their journey from oceanic blue to blood red, two dancers navigate the complexity of a relationship evolving over time. Augenblick is a series of three short films featuring two dancers (Carlos Osantinsky and Fernando Pelliccoli) with an uncanny ability to remain permeable to each other’s provocations without losing their own individuality. The German word “Augenblick,” which might be translated to “blink of an eye,” invokes both the moment and its ephemerality. Once you are aware of being in the moment, it is already over. Partners for over 20 years, Carlos Osantinsky and Fernando Pelliccoli are Argentine dancers living in Berlin who offer improvisation workshops through their company espaciopropio.augenblick. These tenderly playful duets, filmed in Berlin by American filmmaker Juliet McMains, offer insights from their decades-long practice of embodied exploration about the world through the body’s mutable boundaries.
memberships.parsedTitle: Augenblick: On the Edge of the Moment

shorts.description: After 55 years, The Grand Illusion Cinema in Seattle’s University District moved out of its original location. In 2023, the building that housed the cinema for decades was sold for $2.3 million, and the new landlord declined to renew their lease beyond February 2025. As The Grand Illusion searches for a new home, its vibrant history and legacy will live on.
shorts.title: Vanishing Seattle Presents: The Grand Illusion Cinema

shorts.description: Alex’s grandfather is dying of stomach cancer. When the old man starts claiming those aren’t tumours, but pilfered diamonds from a long-forgotten heist in the old country, family secrets and myths collide as Alex grapples with her newfound inheritance resting in a dying man’s stomach.
shorts.title: Diamond Belly

shorts.description: Romance blossoms when a new hire starts at the office. However, nothing can start until someone musters up the courage to make a move.
shorts.title: Hiroshi and Miss. Fujitome

shorts.description: After 45 years, a second-generation filmmaker embarks on a mission to rediscover her mother’s roots and save what’s left of her family’s fading memories of their refugee journey to Canada. To do so, she must overcome one of the greatest challenges for every Asian kid – talking to their parents about the past.
shorts.language: English and Yue Chinese (Cantonese) with English Subtitles
shorts.title: Paper Trail

shorts.description: To Dress a Wound is a poetry-driven experimental short exploring Black girl grief, rage, and daydreams, examining the emotional weight Black women and femmes carry under racial capitalism and patriarchy, and tracing how these histories live within the body across generations. The film explores a diasporic understanding of memory, including language. In moments of ancestral dialogue, Haitian Kreyol, Twi, and Lingala emerge. Subtitles remain in their original languages as an intentional choice.
shorts.title: To Dress a Wound

shorts.description: An adoptee filmmaker invites their adoptive mother, birth mother, and nanny to make a film about ritual, relationship, separation, and reunion.
shorts.language: in English, Filipino (Tagalog), and Ibanag with English Subtitles

shorts.description:
Seattle Premiere!
Defying evacuation orders and denying scientific evidence, notorious lodge owner Harry R. Truman is sent cascading through memories of a life lived without regret on Spirit Lake, as mounting tremors rock his cherished world. Still basking in the limelight of his rebellion, imminent cataclysm calls him to finally face the bet he made against the very force of nature he built his life around.

shorts.description: After risking everything to keep his climbing gym alive, the child of immigrants wrestles with purpose, sacrifice, and his calling to create a space of belonging for others.

shorts.description: Passing through multiple layers of transformation on their journey from oceanic blue to blood red, two dancers navigate the complexity of a relationship evolving over time. Augenblick is a series of three short films featuring two dancers (Carlos Osantinsky and Fernando Pelliccoli) with an uncanny ability to remain permeable to each other’s provocations without losing their own individuality. The German word “Augenblick,” which might be translated to “blink of an eye,” invokes both the moment and its ephemerality. Once you are aware of being in the moment, it is already over. Partners for over 20 years, Carlos Osantinsky and Fernando Pelliccoli are Argentine dancers living in Berlin who offer improvisation workshops through their company espaciopropio.augenblick. These tenderly playful duets, filmed in Berlin by American filmmaker Juliet McMains, offer insights from their decades-long practice of embodied exploration about the world through the body’s mutable boundaries.
shorts.title: Augenblick: On the Edge of the Moment

shorts.description: When a wildfire threatens their home, a struggling artist and his more conventional partner are forced to confront their feelings about security, creativity, and each other.

shorts.description: A cynical filmmaker hired to produce infomercials for a group devoted to the mythical “Mallworld” becomes captivated by their lonely dream of finding a place where they truly belong.

shorts.description: Sound Again is about a boy with degenerative hearing loss who decides, at the age of 12, to get cochlear implants. The procedure renders him technically deaf without the appliance (hearing devices), but leads to a new kind of “hearing.” Almost as a joke, he takes a high school music engineering class and discovers an unexpected talent for music. Incredibly, he becomes a talented, charismatic musician.
shorts.title: Sound Again

shorts.description: A documentary-tinged, meta-fiction bonanza about art, life, and the nature of performance. Simultaneously, a comedic love letter to Los Angeles: as a place, an idea, and a reluctant dream that the filmmaker investigates through gestures both intimate and antagonistic.
